title: The Virtue of Friday
summary: Why Jumu'ah holds a special place in the week.
body: Friday holds a distinct status in Islam, centered on the communal Jumu'ah prayer that replaces the midday prayer for those attending it. Beyond the obligation itself, many Muslims treat Friday as an occasion for extra reflection — reciting Surah Al-Kahf, increasing in supplication, and taking a moment to slow down in the middle of the week. The communal nature of the Jumu'ah prayer is part of its significance: it is a weekly gathering that reconnects individuals to their local community, in a way the five daily prayers, often performed individually, do not always provide. Treating Friday as a slightly different day — rather than an ordinary one — is a small, achievable way to build more rhythm into a week.

title: The Importance of Sincerity in Worship
summary: Why the intention behind an act often matters as much as the act itself.
body: Ikhlas, sincerity, is the idea that acts of worship are meant to be done for the sake of God alone, without seeking praise or recognition from others. It is easy to focus only on whether an act of worship was performed correctly — the right words, the right movements — while giving less thought to why it was performed. Islamic teaching consistently returns to intention as the starting point of any act: a well-known hadith opens with the statement that actions are judged by their intentions. Practically, this means it can be worth pausing, occasionally, to ask not just "did I do this?" but "why did I do this?" — a habit that tends to deepen the meaning of worship over time rather than leaving it as routine.
